Warm-ups for ACL-injury prevention are a well-studied area. The programs built for soccer players (FIFA 11+ is the best known) follow the same pattern: easy jogging, then strength work like Nordic hamstring curls and single-leg balance, then plyometrics with soft, controlled landings, then fast change-of-direction work. The cue that runs through all of it is to land quietly with your knees tracking over your toes, not caving in. They take around 15 to 20 minutes, and the research shows the benefit comes from doing them consistently, two or three times a week or before every session.

If you're coming back from an ACL injury or surgery, or something in the knee is bothering you, that is one for your doctor or physio, not a coach, and they should decide what you're cleared to do and when.

If you want this built into your training, I can build a soccer-ready warm-up and leg days around your knees. Tell me what you want to avoid and the engine will build it.
